_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the adsorption energy of atomic oxygen on Cu(111) at its most stable site, referenced to an isolated O atom.

method.protocol: 0 K static relaxations (BFGS, fmax 0.005 eV/A). E_ads = E(O/slab) - E(slab) - E(O atom, isolated in 20 A box). Bulk Cu a0 relaxed with MLIP (3.640 A). Cu(111) p(3x3) slab, 4 layers, bottom 2 fixed, 16 A vacuum, O at 1/9 ML. Sites tried: fcc, hcp, ontop, bridge (bridge relaxes to fcc). Checks: p(4x4)x4, p(3x3)x5 (3 fixed), p(2x2)x4.
method.ensemble: static 0 K (no ZPE, no thermal corrections)

payload.note:
Most stable site: fcc hollow, O height 1.06 A above top Cu plane. E_ads vs isolated O atom (eV) fcc/hcp/ontop: p(3x3)x4 -4.837/-4.783/-3.082; p(4x4)x4 -4.845/-4.784/-3.078; p(3x3)x5 -4.838/-4.783/-3.081; p(2x2)x4 (0.25 ML) -4.904/-4.839/-3.127. fcc is favoured over hcp by 0.05-0.06 eV in every cell; ontop is not competitive. Same result vs 1/2 O2(g) from the MLIP: -1.69 eV (fcc, 1/9 ML).
PREMISE: this is a well-defined 0 K electronic binding energy, but it cannot be measured directly. An isolated-atom reference is at the edge of what an MLIP covers, because training sets contain no isolated atoms. I tested it below instead of assuming it works.
VALIDATION (same model and settings): (1) Cu cohesive energy vs the MLIP isolated Cu atom = 3.50 eV/atom vs experiment 3.49 eV/atom (Kittel). (2) O2: d = 1.235 A (exp 1.207 A); De = 2E(O) - E(O2) = 6.28 eV vs experiment ~5.21 eV (D0 = 5.12 eV + ZPE). The ~1.1 eV overbinding is the known PBE error for O2. So the MLIP behaves like spin-polarized PBE: its O-atom energy is PBE-like, not an arbitrary fitted E0. (3) Cu a0 = 3.640 A vs exp 3.615 A (RT), the usual PBE overestimate. (4) The fcc > hcp >> top site ordering and the ~1.7 eV binding vs 1/2 O2 agree qualitatively with published GGA studies of O/Cu(111); I did not reproduce a specific published number.
UNCERTAINTY (+/-0.6 eV, total): (a) numerical, from cell size, coverage at <=1/9 ML and slab thickness: <=0.01 eV; at 0.25 ML the value is 0.07 eV more negative. (b) MLIP vs its PBE parent: about 0.1-0.2 eV (estimate, not measured here). (c) The dominant term is PBE vs reality in the O-atom reference. PBE overbinds O2 by ~1.07 eV, i.e. ~0.5 eV per O. A thermochemical alternative uses the MLIP E_ads vs 1/2 O2 plus 1/2 the experimental De: -1.69 - 2.61 = -4.30 eV. The +/-0.6 eV covers both the direct PBE-like value (-4.84) and this corrected estimate (-4.30). No ZPE or finite-temperature terms are included (O ZPE about 0.05 eV).

summary: O/Cu(111) adsorption_energy = -4.84 eV via ASE 3.29 + mace-torch 0.3.15 (MACECalculator, CUDA, float64)/MACE-MPA-0 medium (MPtrj+sAlex, PBE/PBE+U level) 0 K static relaxations (BFGS, fmax 0.005 eV/A). E_ads = E(O/slab) - E(slab) - E(O atom, isolated in 20 A box). Bulk Cu a0 relaxed with MLIP (3.640 A). Cu(111) p(3x3) slab, 4 layers, bottom 2 fixed, 16 A vacuum, O at 1/9 ML. Sites tried: fcc, hcp, ontop, bridge (bridge relaxes to fcc). Checks: p(4x4)x4, p(3x3)x5 (3 fixed), p(2x2)x4.
